messages:
alex.sales: Heads-up, ACME POC hitting ~800ms first-token latency after warmup. Prefill seems not applied and throughput drops on bursts. Anyone who knows prefill/KV behavior? Need to keep demo within SLA.

maria.eng-runtime: ack. Can you paste a sample request + headers? Are you on Dedicated or Hosted?

alex.sales: Hosted (eu-west). Sample: `model: redwood-v2`, `max_tokens:512`, `prefill:true`, route `/v1/generate`. Headers include `X-Client-Id: acme-123` and we pass an `x-api-key`.

sam.eng-ml: Any auth failures around KMS? If prefill keys can't decrypt, runtime will skip KV restore and you get cache miss + regen. Check logs for `prefill:kv:decrypt_error` or `kv:miss`.

alex.sales: I grabbed the last error block from logs: 
```
[2026-03-20T15:02:11Z] request=acme-req-42 route=/v1/generate info="prefill: start"
[2026-03-20T15:02:11Z] warn request=acme-req-42 kv=restore status=failed err="kms_decrypt: permission denied"
[2026-03-20T15:02:11Z] info request=acme-req-42 kv=miss fallback=regenerate
[2026-03-20T15:02:12Z] info request=acme-req-42 token=first  latency=812ms
```

toni.se: That `kms_decrypt: permission denied` usually means the customer KMS key policy or our service principal doesn't have decrypt. Is this the Private/VPC KMS or Hosted key?

alex.sales: It's customer-managed KMS tied to their Dedicated account, they thought they granted `redwood-inference-service` decrypt but maybe misconfigured. They asked if this impacts billing since regeneration costs tokens.

linda.support: Billing wise the tokens are charged as usual. But main blocker is correctness and latency. For a quick demo workaround, you can toggle `prefill:false` to avoid broken restore and warm the model with a short baseline request (e.g., `system: warmup`) to reduce first-token for the demo. Not ideal for production.

maria.eng-runtime: Long-term fix: confirm KMS key policy includes `kms:Decrypt` for the RW service principal and that ARN matches. Also check our audit logs for `Encrypt`/`Decrypt` calls to KMS. I can run a smoke decrypt from our side if we get temporary ARN.

sam.eng-ml: Also check batching window: the client's burst pattern is causing requests to be batched with heterogeneous seq-len which can increase latency for short prompts. Consider reducing `max_batch_latency_ms` on their route or enable fast-path for short sequences.

alex.sales: They're asking about pricing impact if we force prefill to regenerate every request vs fixing KMS. Any rough numbers?

linda.support: Regenerating prefill every request multiplies token usage: if prefill is ~150 tokens and they do 1000 reqs/hr that's 150k extra tokens/hr. Multiply by our hosted per-token price tier. I'll DM a cost estimate.

ops-bot: deploy 1768a7 triggered by maria.eng-runtime — run: `kv-prefill-smoke` on cluster eu-west-1 (status: queued).

maria.eng-runtime: I'll follow up with ACME SRE to get KMS policy screenshots. If they want immediate low-latency demo we can switch them to a small Dedicated pool in eu-west (reserved warm workers) — that avoids shared cold effects but still needs KMS fix for KV restore.

alex.sales: OK doing two things: 1) ask ACME to verify KMS policy, 2) toggle prefill=false for demo and run warmup requests. I'll sync with Toni about getting a temporary Dedicated trial. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam.eng-ml: FYI if you do the warmup, use payloads that match production prompt shapes; short system prompts don't always populate KV the same way.

alex.sales: noted — will copy production prompt. Closing thread once they confirm KMS update.
